title: Ban on Taser guns urged
article: Canada's leading safety group wants the federal government to probe police use of Taser guns, following the deaths of three people in B.C. and one in Ontario shot with the high-voltage devices.

On May 1, Roman Andreichikov died after Vancouver police shot him with a Taser. Last year, Terry Hanna died of cardiac arrest after Burnaby RCMP used a Taser on him, and Clayton Willey died after Prince George RCMP shot him with the device.
On Saturday, former semi-pro boxer Jerry Knight died in Ontario after police used a Taser to subdue him.

"If police continue to use them and people continue to die because they're being shot by them, we have a very, very big public safety issue," said Emile Therien, president of the Canada Safety Council. "There are no independent studies that affirm their safety."
Taser International says the guns are not responsible for deaths in custody.
As incidents mount of people dying after Taser shocks, police forces may face lawsuits, Therien said.
"If you're killed by one of these or severely injured, there's the whole issue of liability," he said. "Who should be using them? Maybe SWAT teams only or highly specially trained individuals."
Vancouver police have 40 Tasers for patrol officers and 10 for Emergency Response Team members. Officers undergo two days of Taser training, said Const. Sarah Bloor.

"Have they saved lives? Yes. In some cases somebody's been armed and we've been able to incapacitate them. Otherwise we would have had to use lethal force," Bloor said. "We can get that person into custody without causing a huge tragedy."
Vancouver police started using the guns four years ago after a coroner's inquest into the shooting death of a mentally ill man, Bloor said.

Willey and Andreichikov were high on cocaine when shot with a Taser. Some people may be more susceptible to injury or death from Taser shocks, Therien said: "If you have high blood pressure, or you wear a pacemaker, or if you're on drugs, it could be different strokes for different folks."
